procedural_matters: Since the request was alleging a breach of RRS 69, prior to the hearing the International Jury appointed an investigator (Mathias Rebholz) in accordance with RRS 69.2(c). The investigator disclosed all relevant information to the panel of the International Jury. The International Jury decided not to call a hearing in accordance with RRS 69.2(e). Having considered all information received from the investigator, the International Jury decided to call a hearing to determine whether Thomas Ruegge had broken a rule, in accordance with RRS 62.1.
Mathias Rebholz (member of the international jury) presented the allegations.
Thomas Ruegge attended the hearing representing himself.
Alexandre Kowalski gave evidence as a witness.
facts: After theraces concluded on June 23rd, while boats were returning from the racing area, a congestion developed at the marina entrance near the breakwater.
Windconditions were light with a small chop.
FRA 222930(Alexandre Kowalski) was connected to his coach boat (Kaspac RIB) and they werewaiting in a queue for the entrance to clear.
Thomas Ruegge, together with the 49erFX crew he was supporting, was waiting astern of FRA 222930. The wing of the supported 49erFX was resting on the tube of ThomasRuegge's RIB.
Thomas Rueggehad his kill cord attached to his leg and the engine of his RIB was running.
At some point, Thomas Ruegge's RIB accelerated unexpectedly. Thomas Ruegge lost his balanceand fell backwards. The kill cord remained attached to his leg and connected withthe kill switch.

ThomasRuegge's RIB surged forward and collided with the coach boat of FRA 222930 and subsequentlystruck FRA 222930 and a Danish 49erFX. As a result of the collision andacceleration, the boom of the Danish 49erFX broke and the sail was ripped.
No personswere injured.

All partiesinvolved gathered immediately after the incident on shore. Thomas Rueggeapologized to all of them, disclosed his insurance details, and cooperatedfully in describing and investigating the incident.
Thomas Rueggestated during the hearing that he is committed to help with furtherinvestigation.

conclusions: By failing tomaintain full control of his RIB and by failing to ensure that his RIB couldnot accelerate inadvertently, whether by accident or through the interventionof a third party, Thomas Ruegge created a risk of dangerous actions, whichconstitutes improper practice, and therefore Thomas Ruegge broke ESTR 4.1.
decision: Using the World Sailing Discretionary Penalty Guidelines for Boats & Support Persons a starting penalty of Level 4 was decided. The penalty was decreased to Level 3 because the breach was accidental and Thomas Ruegge admitted to the breach and contributed to the investigation. Mr. Thomas Ruegge is excluded from going afloat on Wednesday 24th June. The International Jury reminds the Organising Authority to submit a safety incident report to World Sailing.
